title: Feedback spark notebook: mini dossier
content:
TL;DR:
A compact synthesis of customer feedback from Dec 2025 — Jan 2026. Three cross-cutting frictions keep recurring: (1) unpredictability around latency and SLOs across hosted vs dedicated, (2) cost/quality trade-offs for quantized model variants and embeddings, and (3) friction getting Private/VPC deployments networked and tested end-to-end.

Why this note: quick internal reference for PM/SE/CS handoffs. Not exhaustive — this is a working scrapbook intended for rapid probes and to seed a small micro-OKR.

Topline themes (ranked by frequency & escalation risk):
1) Latency predictability (high signal).
   - Platform engineers: want per-route latency SLOs that are actionable (alert thresholds, historical percentiles, and canary gating).
   - Common ask: "How will this behave at 99th pctl under bursty loads (10x baseline)?" Customers expect a deterministic path: if dedicated, we should commit to a tail-latency band.
   - CS evidence: at least 6 mid-market trials asked for an SLA-like metric before moving to committed capacity.
2) Cost vs quality for quantized variants (medium-high).
   - Product teams testing quantized v1 saw 5–8% hallucination rate increase on domain prompts (legal/finance templates). They asked for model-specific guidance (which datasets/benchmarks to run before enabling 4-bit).
   - Repeated request: automated quality checks post-quantize + a small "simulate cost/latency" sandbox.
3) Private/VPC onboarding friction (medium).
   - Networking and certificate churn during customer staging is the most cited blocker to go-live. Engineers want a slim checklist and one-page runbook with preflight validations.

Micro-features and asks (actionable, quick-win focused):
- Route-level fallback matrix UI: let CS/SE declare which model(s) to failover to per-route (example: gpt-j-small -> gpt-j-quant-4 -> gpt-legacy).
- Cost-sim sandbox: small UI where customers run 100 synthetic requests and get an estimated $/1M tokens, latency pctl, and expected quality delta vs baseline.
- Per-token cost attribution in logs: customers want to map cost back to product features (route tags + user_id).
- Prompt-regression hook: tie a small prompt-set to a model rollout and auto-alert if metric (log-likelihood / accuracy) drops > X%.
- Private preflight checklist + automated k8s probe job customers can run (outputs pass/fail + hints).

Persona-specific notes (snippets from field):
- Platform engineering (telco customer): "We need an explicit tail SLO and a way to route all high-priority traffic to dedicated pools during business hours — otherwise our users see variability we can't tolerate."
- Product/ML (startups): "If quantization gives us a 2x price improvement with only a tiny drop for our intents, we'll adopt it — but we need a concrete test harness and recommended hyperparams."
- CS/ops (enterprise): "Private deployment was functionally fine but the network handoff took >6 weeks; we lost momentum. A preflight would have caught cert issues early."

Risk flags / escalations (red/yellow):
- Red: Multiple customers threatened to pause Dedicated commit discussions over tail-latency uncertainty.
- Yellow: Two pilots reported subtle data skew after quantization (ranking problems in search-style prompts).
- Operational: Onboarding docs scatter — inconsistent advice between Console docs and Private deployment README.

Unresolved questions to surface in product sync:
- What is the minimum set of metrics for a "latency SLO" we could provide that is both meaningful and implementable in 60 days? (p50/p95/p99 + CPU/GPU queue length?)
- Can we standardize a small, reproducible quantization checklist for customers to run (dataset size, eval prompts, thresholds)?
- For Private: can we ship a single kubectl-compatible preflight job that validates networking, certs, and routing?

Quick probes (low-cost experiments to run in next 2 sprints):
1) Docs/UX probe: publish a dedicated vs hosted one-pager + checklist and measure CS support threads reduction.
2) Sandbox MVP: internal-only cost-sim script; run with 3 pilot customers and capture feedback.
3) Canary rule experiment: add an optional "failover map" input in the Console for one customer and observe behavior on simulated capacity pressure.
4) Small eval harness: build a 200-prompt dataset for customers in finance/legal to test quantized models and share a simple scoring dashboard.

Immediate next steps (owner suggestions):
- Asha: assemble a 2-page 'hosted vs dedicated latency primer' for customer calls (due 2026-02-10).
- Benji: prototype the cost-sim script + run with 2 mid-market customers (due 2026-02-24).
- Marta: map docs divergence (Console vs repo README) and create a single canonical onboarding checklist (due 2026-02-17).

Notes to self / field scribbles (informal):
- Customer ask language is often "we need SLA" but usually they want predictability and a playbook — the language matters.
- Keep probe scope small; many customers will trade a little extra latency for deterministic behavior if we make failure modes explicit.
- Watch interplay between cache TTL defaults and perceived latency improvements — docs should call out how prefix/KV caching affects repeat queries.

Linked artifacts & anchors: CONFLUENCE-4832 (hosted/dedicated latency primer), JIRA-BH-1287 (prototype cost-sim), JIRA-BH-1299 (preflight job epic), GitHub PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/probe-playbooks/pull/42 (internal probe harness).

Appendix: raw customer quotes (redacted and paraphrased):
- "We can't sign a capacity contract if the third-week 99th percentile is 3x the first-week numbers."
- "Quantized results are close but sometimes the answer shifts from 'no' to 'maybe' in our classifier flow — that's a behavior change we dread."
- "If you give us one test job that validates our networking, we will run it and unblock devs faster."

End of mini dossier. This is intentionally compact; happy to expand any section into a formal PRD or customer-facing checklist once we pick probes.

— Asha
